reveals.label: Cell 1: Visual Diagnostics
reveals.question: 1. What is a karyotype and what does it show?
reveals.expectedAnswer: An ordered visual image of all 46 chromosomes (23 pairs), revealing chromosome number anomalies (aneuploidy) and large structural changes.
reveals.answer: An ordered visual image of all 46 chromosomes (23 pairs), revealing chromosome number anomalies (aneuploidy) and large structural changes.

reveals.label: Cell 2: Chromosome Number
reveals.question: 2. Define the term 'aneuploidy' in human genetics.
reveals.expectedAnswer: An abnormal number of chromosomes in a cell — having extra (e.g. Trisomy 21 = 47) or missing (monosomy = 45) chromosomes.
reveals.answer: An abnormal number of chromosomes in a cell — having extra (e.g. Trisomy 21 = 47) or missing (monosomy = 45) chromosomes.

reveals.label: Cell 3: Inheritance
reveals.question: 3. Differentiate between a dominant and recessive allele.
reveals.expectedAnswer: A dominant allele is expressed with just one copy (Hh, e.g. Huntington's); a recessive allele requires two copies (hh) to be expressed.
reveals.answer: A dominant allele is expressed with just one copy (Hh, e.g. Huntington's); a recessive allele requires two copies (hh) to be expressed.

reveals.label: Cell 4: Cell Biology
reveals.question: 4. What is the normal diploid number of chromosomes in a human somatic cell?
reveals.expectedAnswer: 46 chromosomes (23 homologous pairs: 22 pairs of autosomes + 1 pair of sex chromosomes, XX or XY).
reveals.answer: 46 chromosomes (23 homologous pairs: 22 pairs of autosomes + 1 pair of sex chromosomes, XX or XY).

reveals.label: Cell 5: Probability
reveals.question: 5. Briefly describe the function of a Punnett square.
reveals.expectedAnswer: A grid diagram predicting all possible offspring genotypes, phenotypes, and inheritance probabilities (e.g. 50% Hh : 50% hh) from parental gametes.
reveals.answer: A grid diagram predicting all possible offspring genotypes, phenotypes, and inheritance probabilities (e.g. 50% Hh : 50% hh) from parental gametes.

reveals.label: Cell 6: Monogenic Conditions
reveals.question: 6. Identify one genetic disorder caused by a single gene mutation.
reveals.expectedAnswer: Huntington's disease (HTT gene CAG repeat expansion), Cystic Fibrosis (CFTR), or Sickle Cell Disease (HBB).
reveals.answer: Huntington's disease (HTT gene CAG repeat expansion), Cystic Fibrosis (CFTR), or Sickle Cell Disease (HBB).

slides.title: IVF (In Vitro Fertilisation) — The Gateway to PGT
slides.speakerNotes: Video Checkpoint: How IVF Works | The Story of Fertility | BBC Earth Science — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YWrgyHn0VSY. Emphasise clinical realities: embryos do not always implant; may produce multiple births.

slides.title: Pre-Implantation Genetic Testing (PGT) Subtypes: PGT-A, PGT-M & PGT-SR
slides.speakerNotes: Highlight PGT-M (Monogenic) as the subtype applicable to single-gene disorders such as Huntington's disease (HTT) and Cystic Fibrosis.

slides.title: PGT: The 6-Stage Embryo Biopsy Process
slides.speakerNotes: Step through fertilisation (23+23→46), cleavage (2→4→8 identical cells), single-cell embryo biopsy (does not harm embryo), and selection/implantation of unaffected embryos only.

slides.title: NIPT: Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing (10+ Weeks)
slides.speakerNotes: Video Checkpoint: NIPT (Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing) — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VYlUxaLs3IQ. Maternal arm blood sample taken after 10 weeks analysing placental cell-free fetal DNA (cffDNA) for chromosomal and selected DNA mutations with zero miscarriage risk.

slides.title: Invasive Prenatal Testing: CVS (11–14 wks) vs Amniocentesis (15–20 wks)

Crucial QA note from source deck: A sample of the mother's DNA may also be needed to verify the CVS/amniocentesis result comes strictly from fetal DNA (ruling out maternal cell contamination). Both carry ~0.5–1% miscarriage risk.

objectives.knowledge: Classify clinical genetic tests across Diagnostic, Predictive, and Perinatal pathways (Pre-implantation, Prenatal, Newborn) and map each onto the human developmental timeline (P12).
objectives.application: Explain step-by-step procedures for IVF with Pre-implantation Genetic Testing (PGT-A, PGT-M, PGT-SR), Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing (NIPT after 10 weeks), and Invasive Prenatal Testing (CVS 11–14 wks vs Amniocentesis 15+ wks, including maternal DNA contamination verification) (P12, M7).
objectives.evaluation: Analyse the clinical role, timing, benefits, and risks of each genetic testing modality within Ben's Huntington's disease case study context (M7).

terminology.def: Umbrella clinical category spanning genetic tests around conception, pregnancy, and birth: Pre-implantation (IVF embryos), Prenatal (NIPT, CVS, Amniocentesis), and Newborn screening.

Pre-implantation Genetic Testing subtypes on a single biopsied IVF embryo cell: PGT-A (Aneuploidy / chromosome count), PGT-M (Monogenic single-gene disorders like HD), and PGT-SR (Structural Rearrangements).

Assisted reproduction combining egg and sperm outside the body after hormonal superovulation; embryos are screened and healthy embryos transferred to the uterus (may fail to implant or cause multiple births).
Routine blood draw from the mother's arm after 10 weeks gestation analysing placental cell-free fetal DNA (cffDNA) for chromosomal and selected DNA mutations with zero miscarriage risk.

Invasive ultrasound-guided prenatal diagnostic tests: Chorionic Villus Sampling (placental sample, 11–14 weeks) and Amniocentesis (amniotic fluid fetal cells, after 15 weeks); maternal DNA may be checked to confirm fetal origin.

theoryPoints: Hospital Tests Hook & Card Sort: Distinguish routine hospital diagnostics (imaging, biochemistry, microbiology) from clinical genetic tests grouped into Diagnostic (symptomatic), Predictive (asymptomatic risk), and Perinatal (Pre-implantation, Prenatal, Newborn).

Timing of Genetic Testing Timeline: Egg + sperm fertilisation → Pre-implantation testing (before uterine implantation) → Prenatal testing (during pregnancy: NIPT 10+ wks, CVS 11–14 wks, Amniocentesis 15+ wks) → Newborn screening (at/shortly after birth) → Adult Diagnostic & Carrier/Predictive testing.

Pre-implantation Genetic Testing (PGT-A, PGT-M, PGT-SR) & IVF: Hormonal stimulation yields multiple eggs fertilised in vitro (23 + 23 → 46-chromosome zygote → 2 → 4 → 8 identical cells); a single blastomere/cell is biopsied without harming embryo viability; PGT-M screens single-gene disorders (such as Ben's HTT allele), transferring ONLY unaffected embryos to the uterus (caveats: implantation failure, multiple births).

Non-Invasive vs Invasive Prenatal Testing: NIPT samples maternal arm blood after 10 weeks (cell-free placental DNA in maternal plasma — safe, screens chromosomal/DNA mutations). Invasive CVS (11–14 wks, placental tissue) and Amniocentesis (after 15 wks, amniotic fluid) use ultrasound guidance for definitive fetal DNA diagnosis, often paired with a maternal DNA control sample to rule out maternal cell contamination, weighed against invasive miscarriage risk (~0.5–1%).

OCR P12 & M7 Case Study Application (Ben's HD Family): Ben = Molecular Diagnostic PCR (P12); Unborn 3rd baby = Prenatal testing discussion (NIPT limitations vs definitive invasive CVS/amniocentesis + maternal DNA QA); Future pregnancies = IVF + PGT-M (selecting unaffected hh embryos); 6yo & 3yo children = Predictive testing deferred until adulthood (age 18); Newborn screening = excluded for adult-onset HD.

workedExample.title: Mapping Perinatal & Adult Tests to Ben's Case Study Context (P12 & M7)
workedExample.subtitle: Comparing Diagnostic PCR, PGT-M/IVF, NIPT, CVS, Amniocentesis & Newborn Screening

steps.label: Step 1 — Diagnostic Confirmation for Ben (P12)
steps.detail: Ben is symptomatic at age 40: targeted molecular PCR fragment analysis counts exact HTT exon 1 CAG repeats (≥40 full penetrance) from a routine venous blood sample.

steps.label: Step 2 — Current Pregnancy: NIPT vs Invasive CVS / Amniocentesis (M7)
steps.detail: NIPT (maternal blood after 10 weeks) is non-invasive with zero miscarriage risk (screening cffDNA), whereas invasive ultrasound-guided CVS (11–14 wks, placenta) or Amniocentesis (15+ wks, amniotic fluid) gives definitive fetal CAG sizing — requiring a maternal DNA control check to exclude maternal contamination and carrying ~0.5–1% miscarriage risk.

steps.label: Step 3 — Future Pregnancies & Living Children (M7)
steps.detail: For future children, IVF + PGT-M biopsies a single cell from early 8-cell/blastocyst embryos without harming development and implants only unaffected (hh) embryos (avoiding termination, though implantation is not guaranteed and multiple births can occur). For the 6yo & 3yo, predictive testing is deferred until 18 and newborn screening does not cover HD.

hingeQuestions.question: Which subtype of Pre-implantation Genetic Testing (PGT) is specifically appropriate for screening IVF embryos for a single-gene disorder like Huntington's disease?
options: PGT-M (Monogenic single-gene disorder testing, e.g. HTT allele)
PGT-SR (Structural Rearrangements such as balanced translocations)
hingeQuestions.explanation: PGT-M tests biopsied IVF embryo cells specifically for monogenic (single-gene) inherited conditions like Huntington's disease, whereas PGT-A checks aneuploidy (chromosome number) and PGT-SR checks structural chromosomal rearrangements.

hingeQuestions.question: During invasive prenatal testing (CVS or amniocentesis), why may clinicians also collect a DNA sample from the mother?
options: To measure the mother's blood pressure during the ultrasound scan
To verify that the tested DNA comes strictly from the fetus and has not been contaminated by maternal cells
Because fetal cells do not contain chromosomal DNA until week 30
To replace the need for ultrasound guidance
hingeQuestions.explanation: Comparing a maternal DNA control sample against the CVS (placental) or amniocentesis (amniotic fluid) sample rules out maternal cell contamination, ensuring the diagnostic result truly reflects the fetal genotype.

plenary: Genetic tests follow a clear developmental timeline: Pre-implantation (IVF + PGT-A/M/SR) → Prenatal (NIPT 10+ wks; Invasive CVS 11–14 wks / Amnio 15+ wks) → Newborn screening → Adult Diagnostic & Predictive testing.

PGT-M enables single-cell embryo biopsy without harming development so only unaffected embryos are implanted, while NIPT offers safe 10+ week maternal-blood screening and CVS/Amniocentesis deliver ultrasound-guided invasive diagnosis (with maternal DNA contamination verification).
For OCR P12 and M7, justify molecular PCR diagnosis for Ben and critically analyse the timing, accuracy, and risk trade-offs of every perinatal and adult pathway across his family.
